title: Ginger (Green): modeled ₹1,317/qtl left, Solan → Hamirpur (Nadaun)
summary: January 2025: reported ginger (Green) prices at Solan and Hamirpur (Nadaun) imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 100% of 27 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹1,317 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 582 same-variety market pairs screened for ginger (Green) in January 2025; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Hamirpur (Nadaun) report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2025
scenes.caption: Solan (Himachal Pradesh) and Hamirpur (Nadaun) (Himachal Pradesh) both reported ginger (Green) prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 27 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Solan reported a median ₹4,500 per quintal. Hamirpur (Nadaun) reported a median ₹6,600 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,850/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,850 per quintal, and Hamirpur (Nadaun) was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 189 km by road
scenes.caption: 189 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~3 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹41/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹1,245 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹916 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Hamirpur (Nadaun) report, the rule selects 27 of 27 modeled shipping days. 27 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹1,317 per quintal (₹972 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
